1:
\textbf{(a)} At $x=0$: $y=\sqrt{e^0+\ln1+1}=\sqrt2$. Chain rule:
\[y'=\frac{e^{\sin x}\cos x+\frac{5}{5x+1}}{2\sqrt{e^{\sin x}+\ln(5x+1)+1}},\qquad y'(0)=\frac{1+5}{2\sqrt2}=\frac{3}{\sqrt2}.\]
Tangent line: \boxed{y=\sqrt2+\tfrac{3}{\sqrt2}\,x}.

\textbf{(b)} Differentiate $y^5-x=yx^2+1$:
\[5y^4y'-1=y'x^2+2xy.\]
At $(0,1)$: $5y'-1=0$, so $y'=\frac15$. Tangent line $y\approx1+\frac15x$, so at $x=0.3$:
\[y\approx1+\tfrac15(0.3)=\boxed{1.06}\quad(\text{actual}\approx1.069).\]
2:
\textbf{(a)} $f$ is differentiable everywhere, so by the Mean Value Theorem on $[0,x]$ there is a $c$ in $(0,x)$ with
\[\frac{f(x)-f(0)}{x-0}=f'(c),\ \text{ i.e. }\ f(x)=1+f'(c)\,x.\]
Since $2\le f'(c)\le5$ and $x>0$:
\[\boxed{1+2x\le f(x)\le1+5x}.\]
\textbf{(b)}
\[f'(x)=\frac{2x}{1+x^4}-\frac18\cdot\frac{4x^3}{x^4+1}=\frac{2x-\frac12x^3}{1+x^4}=\frac{x(4-x^2)}{2(1+x^4)}.\]
Critical numbers: $x=0,\ \pm2$. Sign of $f'$: positive on $(-\infty,-2)$, negative on $(-2,0)$, positive on $(0,2)$, negative on $(2,\infty)$.

So $x=-2$ and $x=2$ are \textbf{local maxima}, and $x=0$ is a \textbf{local minimum}.
3:
\textbf{(a)} Quotient rule:
\[f'(x)=\frac{e^x(ax^2+b)-e^x(2ax)}{(ax^2+b)^2}=\frac{e^x(ax^2-2ax+b)}{(ax^2+b)^2}.\]
The denominator is never 0 ($a,b>0$), so the critical numbers solve $ax^2-2ax+b=0$:
\[x=\frac{2a\pm\sqrt{4a^2-4ab}}{2a}=1\pm\sqrt{1-\tfrac ba}.\]
Two real critical numbers exactly when $4a^2-4ab>0$, i.e. \boxed{a>b}.

\textbf{(b)} $\ln f=-\dfrac{\ln x}{x^2}$. Differentiating:
\[\frac{f'}{f}=-\frac{\frac1x\cdot x^2-\ln x\cdot2x}{x^4}=-\frac{1-2\ln x}{x^3}.\]
$f'=0$ when $\ln x=\frac12$, i.e. $x=\sqrt e\approx1.649$ (in the interval). Compare:
\[f(\tfrac12)=\big(\tfrac12\big)^{-4}=16,\quad f(\sqrt e)=e^{-1/(2e)}\approx0.832,\quad f(2)=2^{-1/4}\approx0.841.\]
Absolute maximum \boxed{16} at $x=\frac12$; absolute minimum \boxed{e^{-1/(2e)}\approx0.832} at $x=\sqrt e$.
4:
\textbf{(a)} By similar triangles $\frac rh=\frac28$, so $r=\frac h4$ and
\[V=\frac{\pi}{3}\Big(\frac h4\Big)^2h=\frac{\pi h^3}{48},\qquad \frac{dV}{dt}=\frac{\pi h^2}{16}\frac{dh}{dt}.\]
At $h=2$, $h'=\frac13$: $\dfrac{dV}{dt}=\dfrac{4\pi}{16}\cdot\dfrac13=\dfrac{\pi}{12}\approx0.2618$ ft$^3$/min. Also $\frac{dV}{dt}=0.4-c$, so
\[c=0.4-\frac{\pi}{12}\approx\boxed{0.138\ \text{ft}^3/\text{min}}.\]
\textbf{(b)} The bucket holds $\pi\big(\frac12\big)^2(2)=\frac{\pi}{2}\approx1.571$ ft$^3$. Dripping at $c$ from $t=0$, it fills at
\[t=\frac{\pi/2}{0.4-\pi/12}\approx\boxed{11.4\ \text{min}}.\]
5:
\textbf{(a)} Northernmost at $t=0$: $\theta_0=\frac{\pi}{2}$. Counterclockwise at 5 rev/h: $w=10\pi$ rad/h. The center moves from $(0,0)$ to $(4000,6000)$ in 3 h: $a=\frac{4000}{3}$, $b=2000$.

\textbf{(b)} At $t=4.5$: angle $\frac{\pi}{2}+45\pi\equiv\frac{3\pi}{2}\pmod{2\pi}$, so
\[x=6000+4\cos\tfrac{3\pi}{2}=6000,\qquad y=9000+4\sin\tfrac{3\pi}{2}=8996.\]
Velocity: $x'=a-4w\sin(\theta_0+wt)=\frac{4000}{3}+40\pi\approx1458.997$, and $y'=b+4w\cos(\theta_0+wt)=2000$. Slope $\frac{2000}{1458.997}\approx1.3708$:
\[\boxed{y-8996=1.3708\,(x-6000)}.\]
